summary: Environment A evidence for completing the enrollment CRUD lifecycle (list, add/replace, remove) that Phase 7.2 itself named as deferred work.
auditFinding: An operator who enrolled the wrong song, a bad recording, or simply wanted to stop fingerprinting a song had no way to do so short of manually deleting files inside the app's data directory. See docs/phase-7-3-audit.md and docs/phase-7-3-remove-enrollment.md.
designChoice: No genuine architectural fork - direct completion of the CRUD lifecycle Phase 7.2 started. One real decision, resolved by precedent: manifest-entry removal is unconditional/authoritative (it governs recognition), file deletion is best-effort and non-fatal (logged as a warning, never blocks the command), matching enroll_one's own per-file failure isolation.

newCode.commandsRs: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs: remove_acoustic_reference(song_id) - reads the manifest, errors with an honest 'no enrollment found' AppError if song_id names no entry, writes back the filtered list, then best-effort deletes the entry's audio file (delete failure logged as a warning, never surfaced as a command error). No new crate-level function - composes Phase 7.2's read_manifest_entries/write_manifest_entries as-is.
newCode.libRs: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs: registered commands::remove_acoustic_reference in the invoke handler.
newCode.frontend: commands.ts's removeAcousticReference(songId); LiveChurchBrain.tsx's enrolled-recordings list gains a per-entry Remove button, restructured onto the existing .live-brain__suggestion-header flex-row pattern already used elsewhere in the Music Intelligence panel.

newTests.testingBoundaryRationale: Matches this codebase's established discipline (commands.rs's test module header, reaffirmed in docs/phase-7-3-audit.md): thin command bodies orchestrating already-tested crate-level logic are not separately unit-tested at the Tauri-command layer. install_whisper_model and enroll_acoustic_reference follow the same rule. read_manifest_entries/write_manifest_entries's round-trip and full-replace semantics are already proven in cip-integrations-music-acoustic's Phase 7.2 suite.
frontendNewTests: rejects listAcousticEnrollments/enrollAcousticReference/removeAcousticReference outside the Tauri runtime, without calling invoke() (extended existing test)
newTests.command: cargo test -p cip-integrations-music-acoustic && npm run test -- --run

fullRegression.clippy: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean, both feature configs (default and --features whisper)
fullRegression.check: cargo check --workspace: clean, both feature configs
fullRegression.test: cargo test --workspace: all crates passing, both feature configs, zero regressions (cip-integrations-music-acoustic stable at 48 tests, matching the audit's explicit no-new-crate-tests decision)
fullRegression.frontend: npm run typecheck/lint/test/build: all clean - same 5 pre-existing lint warnings as before this phase, no new ones

architecturalSafetyNotes: Exactly one new Tauri command (remove_acoustic_reference), zero new events, zero new database schema, zero new crate-level functions.
core/music (the domain contract crate) is untouched.
list_acoustic_enrollments/enroll_acoustic_reference and every existing acoustic-recognition code path are byte-identical to before this phase.
remove_acoustic_reference never mutates AppState.acoustic_recognizer - the currently-active recognizer is unaffected until the next restart, matching enrollment's own restart-required discipline.

File deletion is strictly ordered after the manifest write succeeds: an entry can never be left half-removed (present in the manifest but its file already gone), and a file-delete failure never leaves the manifest entry behind.
honestLimitation: No confirmation prompt before removing - the Remove button acts immediately, matching every other operator-decision button in this panel (Accept/Reject on findings). Still no real recorded audio anywhere in this repository or container to actually exercise enroll-then-remove end to end against a genuine acoustic match.
